findings.title: Missing double-check after acquiring write lock
findings.body: GetWebAssets releases the RLock before checking whether the cache is populated, then unconditionally re-reads the manifest after taking the write lock. Two concurrent callers that both observe a nil cache will both serialize on the write lock and each perform the full file read and JSON parse, instead of the second caller reusing the value just populated by the first. Adding a re-check of `entryPointAssetsCache` after the Lock() (classic double-checked locking) would eliminate the redundant I/O on the cold-start path. Not a correctness bug—safe under the mutex—but wasteful for concurrent first callers in production.

findings.title: No regression test added for the data race fix
findings.body: The PR's stated purpose is to fix a data race on the shared `entryPointAssetsCache` global, but no test exercising concurrent calls to GetWebAssets is included. For a race-condition fix, the maintainer should expect at least one test that invokes GetWebAssets from multiple goroutines (intended to be run with `go test -race`) to guard against the race being reintroduced. Without such a test, the fix is verified only by inspection and there is no automated guard against future regressions on this exact path.
